text: Git is a version control system that helps developers manage changes to their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. For example, you can create a feature branch to add a new function safely. When your work is ready, you merge the branch back into the main project. In team projects, developers often open a pull request before merging. This lets others review the code and suggest improvements. Following a clear version control workflow with branches, merging, and pull requests keeps projects organised and reduces mistakes.
